props.label: Main
props.html:
Registered NDIS provider, Sydney and Perth

NDIS Provider in Sydney and Perth for Complex and Clinical Care

For people whose support includes clinical care, and for the coordinators who place them.

Abundance Healthcare Group is a registered NDIS provider in Sydney and Perth for people with complex and clinical needs. Registered nurses design and oversee every care plan, and we tell you plainly, within one business day, whether we have the capacity to take a referral on.

Who we are

A nurse-led NDIS provider for people with high and complex needs

Abundance Healthcare Group is an NDIS service provider in Sydney and Perth that specialises in complex care at home. We support participants who need clinical tasks such as tube feeding, bowel care, catheter care and wound care, with registered nurses writing the plans and training the workers.

Most providers are set up for everyday support. We are set up for the cases that carry clinical risk: someone coming home from hospital with a feeding tube, a person with a progressive condition whose needs change month to month, a family who has been told the care is too complex. We work as an NDIS support provider in two cities, Sydney and Perth, and we are based in Campbelltown.

  • Registered nurses behind the care plan and the clinical tasks
  • Support workers trained and signed off for each high intensity task
  • Clear escalation when a participant's condition changes

You can read about the team behind the care and how the business is run.

What we specialise in

Complex and clinical supports we deliver

We deliver four groups of support: high intensity daily personal activities, community nursing in the home, daily personal care with clinical backup, and community access and transport. Each is delivered under our NDIS registration, and most participants use more than one.

High intensity daily personal activities

Personal care that needs specific training, such as complex bowel care, PEG feeds and catheter care, delivered by trained workers under a nurse's plan. Read about high intensity daily personal activities.

Explore

Community nursing in the home

Wound care, catheter changes, medication management and clinical assessment from a registered nurse. See how we provide nursing care delivered at home.

Explore

Daily personal care with clinical backup

Showering, dressing, meals and transfers from workers who know the clinical plan and can call the nurse when something changes. See our daily personal care.

Explore

Community access and transport

Support to reach appointments, treatment and community life, with the same workers who provide care at home. See our community access support.

Explore

Not sure where a task fits? The page on the clinical tasks we are registered to deliver sets out what we take on and what we do not, or you can see every service in one list.

Who we support

Who we support

We support people whose disability means complex, changing or clinically involved care. Most of the people we work with live with a progressive neurological condition, a spinal cord or brain injury, cerebral palsy, or a psychosocial disability alongside physical health needs.

  • Motor neurone diseaseSupport that steps up as needs change
  • Progressive neurological conditionsMS, Parkinson's and Huntington's disease
  • Spinal cord injuryBowel, bladder and skin routines
  • Acquired brain injuryRoutine and support after rehabilitation
  • Psychosocial disabilityConsistent workers and daily structure
  • Cerebral palsyAdults with high physical support needs

Our work centres on participants with complex and high intensity needs. For a fuller picture, see the conditions we support.

Find the right support

Which NDIS support do you need?

The right support depends on the task and who is allowed to do it. Tasks with clinical risk need a trained worker or a nurse. Everyday help with showering, dressing and getting out does not. The table matches common needs to the support type and its NDIS registration group.

What is neededSupport typeWho delivers itRegistration group
Tube feeds, bowel care, catheter care or set injections every dayHigh intensity daily personal activitiesSupport worker trained on the task, under a nurse's plan0104 Assist Personal Activities High
Wound dressings, catheter changes, nurse-only medication, care planningCommunity nursing careRegistered nurse0114 Community Nursing Care
Showering, dressing, meals and transfersDaily personal careSupport worker0107 Assist-Personal Activities
Travel to appointments, treatment and community activitiesTransport and community accessSupport worker who drives0108 Assist-Travel/Transport

Why it is different

Why families and coordinators choose a nurse-led provider

Families and coordinators choose a nurse-led provider because someone clinically qualified is accountable for the plan. Tasks are done the same way every shift, a change in condition is noticed early, and there is one person to call when something is not right.

Registered with the NDIS Commission

We are a registered NDIS provider, Registration ID 4-JCLD6XE. The Commission's public register lists our registration groups, including high intensity personal activities and community nursing care. If you want to check that an NDIS provider in Sydney is registered, the register is the place to confirm it.

A registered nurse behind every complex plan

A registered nurse assesses each participant, writes a plan for every clinical task, trains the workers and reviews the plan after any hospital stay or change in health.

A straight answer on capacity

We reply to every enquiry within one business day with a yes, a no or a start date. Overnight and round the clock rosters are confirmed case by case, and we do not accept a referral we cannot staff safely.

For referrers

For support coordinators and hospital discharge planners

We work with support coordinators and discharge planners who need to place a participant with clinical needs. You send the referral, we confirm capacity within one business day, a nurse assesses, and you receive written updates after each review.

The hardest part of placing a complex participant is finding out early whether a provider can really do it. We publish what we deliver, answer quickly and put it in writing. There is information for referrers on how we handle intake and reporting, or you can refer a participant now.

Locations

Where we deliver care across Sydney and Perth

We deliver care in participants' homes across Greater Sydney and the Perth metropolitan area. Our office is at 39 Chamberlain St, Campbelltown, and Sydney teams work across the west, south west, south, inner city, east and north, wherever trained workers are available.

Greater Sydney

From Campbelltown we cover eight regions of the city. See disability services across Sydney for each region and council area.

Perth

We support participants across the Perth metropolitan area. See NDIS support in Perth for the areas covered and how to enquire.

People often look for an NDIS provider near me and find a long list with little detail. Tell us the suburb and we will say whether trained workers are available there.

Reviews

What clients and referrers say on Google

Reviews of Abundance Healthcare Group are public on our Google Business Profile. We do not quote, score or summarise them on this page, so you can read what families and referrers have written in their own words and judge for yourself.

Read our reviews on Google

Common questions

Questions people ask before choosing an NDIS provider

Is Abundance Healthcare Group a registered NDIS provider?

Yes. Abundance Healthcare Group is registered with the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, Registration ID 4-JCLD6XE. Our registration groups include high intensity personal activities and community nursing care, and anyone can confirm them on the Commission's public register.

What makes a complex care provider different from a general NDIS provider?

A complex care provider has registered nurses who assess participants, write clinical plans and train workers for tasks such as tube feeding, bowel care and catheter care. A general provider delivers everyday support and usually refers clinical tasks elsewhere.

Do you have capacity for a new high intensity or overnight participant?

It depends on the suburb, the supports and the hours. We answer every enquiry within one business day. Overnight and round the clock rosters are confirmed case by case, because they need several trained workers living near the participant.

Which parts of Sydney and Perth do you cover?

Greater Sydney and the Perth metropolitan area. In Sydney we work from our Campbelltown office across the west, south west, south, inner city, east and north. Give us the suburb and we will confirm whether trained workers are available.

How are your supports funded in an NDIS plan?

Mostly from the Core Supports budget. Personal care and high intensity support come under Assistance with Daily Life, nursing is funded as a disability-related health support, and community trips come from the community participation or transport budgets. We charge within the NDIA's current price limits.

How quickly will you respond to an enquiry or referral?

Within one business day. You will get a clear answer on whether we can take the referral, and if so, the likely start date and what we need from you to arrange the nurse's assessment.

Can families self refer, or does a coordinator need to refer?

Either. Participants and families can contact us directly, and so can support coordinators, plan managers and hospital discharge planners. We need the plan dates, the supports required and any recent clinical documents.

For background reading on funding, high intensity supports and nursing, see our NDIS guides.
